text: Rice harvesting (ការប្រមូលផលស្រូវ) is one continuous process: cutting, threshing (ការបោកស្រូវ), cleaning (ការសម្អាតស្រូវ), drying (ការហាល/សម្ងួតស្រូវ), and protecting grain from contamination and rain. Cambodian guidance recommends harvesting at roughly 80-85% straw-colored grains, with lower panicle grains hard rather than soft; harvesting too early gives immature, chalky grain, too late increases shattering and cracking. The practical method depends on available labor and machinery: manual cutting and later threshing, or a hired mobile thresher/combine where available. Mechanical equipment must be properly adjusted -- excessive threshing or poor settings cause broken/cracked grain, while under-threshing leaves grain still attached. During the wet season and its transition to drier months, weather is a major source of post-harvest loss: don't leave freshly cut rice lying on wet soil, and minimize time between cutting and threshing. Dry paddy as soon as possible after threshing (ideally within about 24 hours) since high-moisture paddy deteriorates quickly (mold, discoloration, insects, reduced milling quality). Traditional sun-drying on clean mats, tarpaulins, or clean surfaces remains realistic for smallholders, but the farmer needs a rain contingency plan and should never dry grain directly on contaminated ground. Do not assume mechanical drying is available -- ask whether a nearby rice mill, trader, or cooperative offers a shared drying service before assuming the farmer needs to buy one. Do not infer harvest date solely from variety name; combine variety-specific maturity guidance (when known) with field maturity indicators, weather, and the farmer's actual harvesting/drying capacity before advising them to harvest.
